chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Sama'a, from 'Abdullah ibn Jabala, from 'Ala', from Muhammad, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), said:

I asked him about the Sa'ibah (a female slave freed by her master) and the one who was from the People of the Covenant (Dhimmi), if one of them married a Muslim on the condition that he pays the blood-money (diyah) for her, and thus her inheritance becomes his, is that permissible? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ اَلذِّمَّة: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.اَلسَّائِبَة: A female slave freed by her master, often with specific inheritance rules
key_terms.وَالَى: To marry or take in marriage; to establish guardianship
key_terms.يَعْقِلَ: To pay the blood-money (diyah) on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a Muslim man to marry a free non-Muslim woman or a Sa'ibah if he agrees to pay her blood-money?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the inheritance rights in a mixed-faith marriage where a free woman (specifically a *Sa'ibah* or a *Dhimmi*) marries a Muslim under the condition that he assumes her *diyah* (blood-money) liability. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of this arrangement, establishing that the husband’s assumption of financial responsibility validates the inheritance link, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Kitabah* and marital contracts with non-Muslims.
